name: openGym
description: Self-hosted gym & body-weight tracker — plan routines, log workouts (supersets, warm-ups, cardio), see which muscles are trained, fatigued or detrained, import from FitNotes/Strong/Hevy, passkey login. Your data, your server.
one_liner: A workout and gym-tracking app you run yourself on your own server, instead of trusting a company's app with your fitness data or paying a subscription.
buyer: A privacy-conscious fitness enthusiast or a small personal-training business that wants to offer clients a branded workout tracker without being locked into a SaaS fitness app.
business_use_cases: A personal trainer self-hosts it and gives clients passkey logins to a branded version to plan and log their programs.
A privacy-focused fitness user runs it on a home server instead of paying for subscription apps like Strong or Hevy.
A boutique gym offers it as a member perk: members get a tracker tied to the gym's own programs instead of a generic app.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a managed, hosted version for personal trainers and small gyms who don't want to run their own server, with white-labeling.
Sell a 'migrate and set up' service for people moving off FitNotes, Strong or Hevy who want it self-hosted but don't want to do the Docker setup themselves.

steal_this: This weekend, spin up a hosted instance for a local personal trainer's clients and charge a small monthly fee to manage hosting and backups for them.
